ai.description: Calamaria pavimentata is a slender snake reaching 30 cm. It is brown above with dark crossbands or spots and a yellow-spotted underside. It features a blunt, shovel-shaped head and a short tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Calamaria pavimentata* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of dark, longitudinal stripes or a series of small, dark, rectangular spots on a brownish body.
ai.habitat: The Brown Reed Snake inhabits moist, shaded forest floors and leaf litter in hilly regions, typically ranging from lowlands up to approximately 2,000 meters in altitude.
ai.behavior: The Brown Reed Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time burrowing through leaf litter and loose soil in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calamaria pavimentata* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–3 eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, often peaking between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calamaria pavimentata* is found in Northeast India, specifically in states like Assam and Meghalaya, typically inhabiting low to mid-elevation forests.
